decisions.statement: A unit is written to a folder akasha owns and reached by a link systemd reads.
A unit akasha installed is a unit whose link points into that folder.
A unit akasha staged is a `.service` or `.timer` file sitting in that folder.
Anything staged there that is neither is no unit and is weighed by nothing.
A staged unit no link reaches and no service accounts for is stranded.
A stranded file is taken away with systemd told to stop and disable nothing.
Anything else sitting beside a unit akasha owns is left alone.
A unit akasha owns that no service accounts for is taken away.
A service that is not to be running is written its unit and stopped rather than taken away.
Only the unit systemd starts the service by is enabled.
systemd is reloaded after the units are written and before any unit is enabled.
A systemctl call that refuses is carried back rather than printed and forgotten.
Nothing here is installed for the whole machine.
Nothing here reads a page.
Nothing here reaches the cluster.
A unit is stopped before that unit is disabled.
Disabling a unit takes away the link akasha reaches that unit by.
A unit written and the link to it are named apart, each after that one landed.
A unit is named removed after its staged file has gone rather than after a disable.
A link that was already there is named by nothing, since nothing wrote it.
A link a disable took away is made again.
systemd is reloaded again where a link was made again.
A unit named to be restarted is restarted after every unit is enabled.
A plan naming no unit to restart restarts nothing.
The pages service is restarted before any other unit named to be restarted.

definition: the units a workstation service is installed as
